lead: Irving plumbing deals with clay soil, slab foundations and a mix of older homes and newer Las Colinas buildings. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Irving.
risk: slab leaks from shifting clay, aging pipes in older homes and burst pipes in freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes and frozen pipes
why: South and central Irving have many homes from the 1950s to the 1970s with cast-iron drains and copper lines under the slab. Expansive clay moves with the seasons and stresses those lines.
Las Colinas and Valley Ranch add condos, offices and newer homes. Rare hard freezes burst attic and exterior-wall pipes across the city.
water: Irving gets water mainly from Lake Chapman, with some bought from Dallas Water Utilities. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Know where your main shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in Las Colinas, Valley Ranch, Downtown Irving, Hackberry Creek, University Hills, Plymouth Park and every other Irving neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Irving Inspections Division, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Where does Irving's water come from?
faq.a: Most comes from Lake Chapman in northeast Texas, carried by pipeline, with some bought from Dallas. It is moderately hard, so scale slowly builds up.
